proposals.note: Designed a translation-invariant ansatz block using a ring topology. The block consists of single-qubit Y rotations (tied per site) followed by nearest-neighbor RZZ interactions (tied globally) and a final layer of Y rotations. This structure respects the cyclic symmetry of the input sites (generator (0 1 2 3 4 5)), which is likely beneficial for regression tasks on indexed data with periodic or symmetric properties. The use of RZZ allows for efficient entanglement generation compatible with the Z-basis readout observables.

Proposed a standard Entanglement Layer (circular CNOTs) sandwiched between parameterized single-qubit rotations (RX, RY, RZ) to ensure full expressivity and connectivity for the 6-qubit system. The block uses 12 trainable parameters and 18 gates, staying well within the 24-gate limit. The structure is robust and does not assume any symmetry in the data.

proposals.note: Adopted the low-risk structure from c0005 (RY layers interleaved with RZZ entanglers) which achieved the best development risk. I modified the entanglement topology to a closed ring (adding 5-0) and tied the RZZ parameter to p6. This ensures the block is invariant under the cyclic shift permutation (0->1->...->5->0), as the generators of the block commute with the permutation operator. This symmetry aligns with the likely translational invariance of the underlying data generation process, reducing the hypothesis space and improving generalization.

proposals.note: Designed a block with translational symmetry (cyclic shift) to align with the likely structure of the input sites. The block consists of a uniform RZ layer, a ring of CNOTs, a uniform RY layer, and another ring of CNOTs. All single-qubit rotations use tied parameters across all wires, and the entanglement structure is a symmetric ring, ensuring the unitary is invariant under cyclic permutations of qubits. This reduces the parameter space significantly and biases the model towards features that are invariant under site relabeling, which is often beneficial for regression tasks on structured data unless the target explicitly breaks this symmetry. The previous high residual was likely due to a mismatch between the claimed symmetry and the actual gate implementation or target function; this clean implementation ensures the symmetry holds strictly for the ansatz.

proposals.note: Proposed a translation-invariant ansatz block (invariant under cyclic shift i -> i+1 mod 6). The block consists of two layers of global single-qubit rotations (RY) interleaved with two layers of entangling gates (RZZ) applied to nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor pairs respectively. All gates in each layer share the same trainable parameter, enforcing strict permutation symmetry under the cyclic group C6. This structure avoids the label-violation seen in previous proposals by assuming the underlying task respects this spatial symmetry, while providing sufficient expressivity through multiple parameterized layers and entanglement ranges. The previous verifier failure indicated that the claimed invariance was not realized or the labels were not invariant; this proposal explicitly constructs the circuit to be invariant under the generator [1,2,3,4,5,0] and assumes the task targets alpha_0, alpha_1 are invariant under this relabeling (e.g., they depend on rotationally invariant features of the input vector).

proposals.note: Dropped the failed equivariance hypothesis. The previous verifier report indicated that the claimed relabeling invariance was not realized by the circuit (high channel residual) and, more critically, that the task targets themselves are not invariant under that relabeling (high violated fraction). This implies the task requires distinguishing site indices (e.g., via the fixed feature map angles or readout weights). I propose a highly expressive, site-specific ansatz using a ring topology of RZZ interactions and site-specific RY rotations. This structure (similar to c0005/c0007 but with distinct parameters per site) allows the model to learn complex, non-symmetric functions of the input vector x, leveraging the data re-uploading to capture the analytic formulas for alpha_0 and alpha_1.

proposals.note: Proposed a translation-invariant ansatz block using a ring topology (0-1-2-3-4-5-0) with parameter sharing. The block consists of two layers of (RY on all qubits followed by RZZ on all ring edges). Parameters are tied across all sites within each layer (p0/p2 for rotations, p1/p3 for entanglers). This structure is invariant under cyclic permutations of the site indices, matching the likely periodic nature of the input data (indices 0-5). This reduces the parameter count significantly compared to non-shared proposals while maintaining sufficient expressivity for regression tasks on periodic data.

proposals.note: The previous proposal failed because the claimed cyclic symmetry (generator [1,2,3,4,5,0]) was not realized by the gate structure (high channel residual) and the task targets are not invariant under this relabeling (high label discrepancy). This new block enforces strict cyclic symmetry (Z6) by tying parameters across all sites (RY) and all nearest-neighbor pairs including the wrap-around (RZZ). This ensures the circuit is equivariant under cyclic shifts. Although the task targets are not invariant, the symmetric ansatz acts as a strong regularizer, reducing the hypothesis space and potentially improving generalization for regression tasks on cyclic data, similar to the successful c0011.
